headline: A 2022 law temporarily loosens some rules on lending or leasing U.S. defense equipment to Ukraine and nearby Eastern European countries affected by Russia's invasion.
what_it_does: The law lets the President lend or lease defense equipment to Ukraine's government or the governments of other Eastern European countries affected by Russia's invasion without certain usual requirements. For fiscal years 2022 and 2023, these agreements are not subject to some rules that normally apply, including the general five-year limit on loan or lease periods. The President must also set up expedited procedures to deliver the equipment on time.

who_it_affects.how: It can receive U.S. defense articles under lend-lease agreements that do not have to meet certain standard requirements, including the five-year limit on loan or lease periods.

who_it_affects.group: Governments of other Eastern European countries affected by Russia's invasion of Ukraine
who_it_affects.how: They may also receive U.S. defense articles under these temporarily modified lend-lease agreements.

who_it_affects.group: The President and executive branch agencies that handle lend-lease transfers
who_it_affects.how: They must follow the waivers for fiscal years 2022 and 2023 and create expedited procedures to deliver the equipment on time.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted May 9, 2022; the temporary waivers apply to fiscal years 2022 and 2023.
